items.definition: To examine data, evidence, or a phenomenon in detail in order to understand its components or draw conclusions.
exampleSentences: The team analysed the survey data to identify significant patterns in consumer behaviour.
Researchers analysed blood samples from over a thousand participants to test the hypothesis.
Before drawing any conclusions, the results must be analysed for statistical significance.

items.definition: To evaluate the extent, quality, or significance of something, typically based on available evidence.
exampleSentences: The study assessed the long-term effects of sleep deprivation on memory retention.
Reviewers were asked to assess the validity of the experimental design before publication.
Researchers use standardized tests to assess cognitive development in young children.

items.definition: To accept something as true or to take it as a starting point for an argument or calculation, without first proving it.
exampleSentences: The model assumes that all variables are independent of one another.
For simplicity, the researchers assumed a constant rate of decay throughout the experiment.
It would be wrong to assume that correlation implies causation.

items.definition: Facts, figures, or observations collected through measurement, experimentation, or observation, used as a basis for analysis.
exampleSentences: The data were collected over a six-month period using standardized questionnaires.
Researchers cross-checked the data against previous studies to confirm the trend.
Missing data can significantly skew the results of a statistical analysis.

items.definition: To state the precise meaning of a term or concept, or to establish the boundaries and characteristics of something.
exampleSentences: The researchers carefully defined each variable before beginning the experiment.
It is difficult to define intelligence in a way that all psychologists accept.
The study's scope was defined by strict inclusion and exclusion criteria.

items.definition: To obtain or trace something from a particular source, or to reach a result through logical or mathematical reasoning.
exampleSentences: The formula can be derived from Newton's second law of motion.
Much of what we know about the disease was derived from early animal studies.
Students were asked to derive the equation step by step rather than memorize it.

items.definition: To calculate or judge the approximate value, size, or extent of something, especially where an exact measurement is not possible.
exampleSentences: Scientists estimate that the species has existed for over two million years.
The initial estimate of the sample size proved too small for reliable results.
Researchers estimated the margin of error at roughly three percent.

items.definition: Clearly visible or understood from the available facts or evidence; obvious.
exampleSentences: It became evident from the data that the treatment had no significant effect.
The correlation between the two variables was immediately evident on the graph.
Despite repeated trials, no clear pattern was evident in the results.

items.definition: A mathematical rule or relationship expressed in symbols, or a fixed method for achieving a particular result.
exampleSentences: The formula relates pressure, volume, and temperature in an ideal gas.
Researchers applied a standard formula to calculate statistical significance.
There is no simple formula for predicting how a chemical reaction will proceed.

items.definition: To recognize, establish, or single out a particular fact, cause, pattern, or entity through observation or analysis.
exampleSentences: The study aimed to identify the genetic factors linked to the disease.
Researchers identified a previously unknown species during the expedition.
The analysis helped identify which variables had the greatest effect on the outcome.

items.definition: To point to a fact or conclusion as being probable, or to show something clearly through signs or evidence.
exampleSentences: The results indicate a strong link between diet and cardiovascular health.
Preliminary data indicate that the new treatment may reduce recovery time.
A rising baseline reading can indicate a fault in the measuring equipment.

items.definition: To explain or determine the meaning or significance of information, data, or behaviour.
exampleSentences: Different researchers interpreted the same data set in strikingly different ways.
The findings must be interpreted with caution given the small sample size.
She was trained to interpret X-ray images for signs of fracture.

items.definition: A particular systematic procedure or set of steps used to carry out a task, especially in research or experimentation.
exampleSentences: The paper describes the method used to isolate the compound.
Researchers adopted a mixed-methods approach, combining surveys with interviews.
A flawed method can undermine even the most promising hypothesis.

items.definition: A series of actions or steps taken to achieve a particular result, or to handle and analyse information systematically.
exampleSentences: The data were processed using specialized statistical software before analysis.
Photosynthesis is the process by which plants convert light into chemical energy.
The peer-review process can take several months before a paper is accepted.

items.definition: The systematic investigation of a subject in order to discover or establish facts and reach new conclusions.
exampleSentences: Her research focuses on the effects of climate change on marine ecosystems.
The team spent three years researching the causes of the disorder.
Further research is needed before any firm conclusions can be drawn.

items.definition: The arrangement of parts within a system, or to organize something according to a particular framework.
exampleSentences: The molecule's structure determines how it interacts with other compounds.
Researchers structured the questionnaire to avoid leading questions.
Understanding the structure of the atom was a turning point in physics.

items.definition: A set of principles or ideas developed to explain observed phenomena, often supported by evidence and used to make predictions.
exampleSentences: The theory of evolution remains the foundation of modern biology.
Her experiment was designed to test a long-standing theory about memory formation.
In theory, the reaction should occur spontaneously at room temperature.

items.definition: To differ or change, especially in size, amount, or degree, from one instance or condition to another.
exampleSentences: Results varied considerably depending on the temperature at which the experiment was conducted.
The concentration of the solution was varied to test its effect on reaction speed.
Response times varied widely among participants of different ages.

items.definition: To calculate a value or result, typically using mathematics or a computer.
exampleSentences: The software computes the standard deviation automatically from the raw scores.
Researchers computed the correlation coefficient between the two variables.
It would take hours to compute the result by hand without a computer.

items.definition: To carry out or organize a particular activity, especially a piece of research, experiment, or investigation, or, in physics, to transmit heat, electricity, or sound.
exampleSentences: The team conducted a series of controlled experiments over two years.
Copper conducts electricity far more efficiently than most other metals.
The study was conducted in accordance with strict ethical guidelines.

items.definition: To build or create something systematically, such as an argument, model, or experiment, or a concept devised for analysis.
exampleSentences: The researchers constructed a mathematical model to simulate population growth.
Intelligence is often treated as a psychological construct rather than a single measurable trait.
A well-constructed experiment controls for as many confounding variables as possible.

items.definition: To assess the value, significance, or quality of something, typically after careful consideration of evidence.
exampleSentences: An independent panel evaluated the study's methodology before it was published.
The trial was designed to evaluate the drug's effectiveness against a placebo.
Researchers must evaluate the reliability of their instruments before collecting data.

items.definition: A distinctive characteristic or attribute of something, or to include something as a prominent element.
exampleSentences: One key feature of the sample was its unusually high genetic diversity.
The study features a much larger control group than earlier research in the field.
Researchers identified several shared features among the surviving specimens.

items.definition: To gain possession of or achieve something, especially through effort, calculation, or a formal process.
exampleSentences: Consent was obtained from all participants before the trial began.
The team obtained consistent results across three separate trials.
Pure samples of the compound are difficult to obtain in the laboratory.

items.definition: A class or division of things regarded as having particular shared characteristics, used to organize or classify data.
exampleSentences: Participants were divided into three categories based on age and activity level.
The species was reclassified into a new taxonomic category after genetic testing.
Researchers coded each response into one of five predefined categories.

items.definition: Consisting of many interconnected parts and therefore difficult to analyse or understand, or a system of closely related parts.
exampleSentences: Climate systems are extremely complex, with countless interacting variables.
The enzyme forms a complex with the substrate during the reaction.
Even a relatively complex model failed to predict the outbreak accurately.

items.definition: A fundamental part or component of something, or, in chemistry, a substance that cannot be broken down into simpler substances.
exampleSentences: Motivation is a key element in any successful learning strategy.
Carbon is the element that forms the basis of all known life.
The researchers isolated each element of the process to study it separately.

items.definition: To regard or represent one thing as being equal, equivalent, or corresponding to another.
exampleSentences: It is misleading to equate correlation with causation in observational studies.
The researchers equated the two groups on age, gender, and education level.
A higher test score should not automatically be equated with greater understanding.

items.definition: Recognizably different or separate from something else in nature, quality, or kind.
exampleSentences: The two subspecies are genetically distinct despite their similar appearance.
Researchers identified three distinct phases in the disease's progression.
The results from the two experiments were distinct enough to rule out coincidence.

items.definition: Conforming to a usual, average, or expected standard, or, in statistics, relating to a symmetrical bell-shaped distribution of data.
exampleSentences: Body temperature outside the normal range can indicate infection.
The data followed a roughly normal distribution, allowing standard statistical tests to be used.
It is normal for measurements to show some degree of variation between trials.
